findings.finding: A4 finding A1 contains an off-by-one in its 'b'-file leg, and the error is propagated verbatim into lane_verdicts.json (binding_ruling_amendment: "'b' files land M+1/14 after 30-day months"; "~46% of half-month files carry a same-day intraday leak window at 16d"). Correct calendar arithmetic on the dossier's own convention (bound = half_month_end + 15 days; usable = half_month_end + guard): for a 30-day month M, M/30 + 15d = M+1/15 (NOT M+1/14), so the 'b'-file posting bound EQUALS the promised M+1/15 for every month length and the 16d guard usable instant M+1/16 is strictly after the promise — 'b' files are CLOSED at a 16d guard in all month lengths. The only leaky class at 16d is 'a' files of 31-day months (promise M/31 vs usable M/15+16 = M/31 = promise day): 7 of 24 half-month file classes ~= 29%, not 11/24 ~= 46%. MATERIALITY: none to the verdict — the binding tightening direction is unchanged and the >=17 calendar day BINDING minimum is CORRECT and still required (it is exactly what closes the 'a'-31day class: usable M+1/01 > promise M/31; 17d closes every class; verified independently). The error overstates the leak surface, never understates it, so no gate is weakened.
findings.required_remediation: Append-only erratum (lane_verdicts.json amendment note or a control-dir erratum file): correct the leaky-class statement to "'a' files of 31-day months only, 7/24 ~= 29%; 'b' files closed at 16d in all month lengths (M/30+15d = M+1/15)"; state that the >=17d BINDING guard stands unchanged. No verdict change; no re-audit required (finding is documentation-accuracy, direction conservative).
